content: If you are a resident of the United States and require assistance, you can contact the Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose: It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as prescribed and on schedule. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. Storage Instructions: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Uses: This product contains two active ingredients, netupitant and palonosetron. It is used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by cancer drug treatments, such as chemotherapy. How to Use: Before starting this medication, read the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Review it again each time you receive a refill. Side Effects: Headaches may occur as a side effect of this medication. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they have determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. One of the active ingredients, palonosetron, may increase serotonin levels and, in rare cases, lead to a serious condition known as serotonin syndrome or serotonin toxicity. The risk of this condition increases if you are taking other medications that elevate serotonin levels. Inform your doctor or pharmacist about all the medications you are taking to avoid potential interactions. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor. Precautions: Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to netupitant, palonosetron, or other anti-nausea serotonin blockers (e.g., ondansetron). Also, disclose any other allergies you may have. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this product passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting how they work. Similarly, other medications may influence the removal of this product from your body, altering its effectiveness. Examples include rifamycins (e.g., rifampin) and St. John’s wort. The risk of serotonin syndrome or toxicity increases if you are taking other drugs that elevate serotonin levels, such as MDMA (ecstasy), certain antidepressants (e.g., SSRIs like fluoxetine or paroxetine, SNRIs like duloxetine or venlafaxine), or others. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose (Reiterated): It is essential to adhere to the prescribed dosing schedule. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to determine the appropriate course of action. Storage (Reiterated): Store the medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly. Final Note: This information was last revised in May 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most accurate and personalized guidance regarding your medications and health conditions.
